title: fix(plugin-list): the capability gate resolves `chart` from a declared chart block (objectui#7544)
body:
Fixes #7544

## What was wrong

`ListView`'s `availableViews` memo builds `resolvable` from each visualization's binding and then intersects it with `appearance.allowedVisualizations` (ADR-0047: whitelist ∩ resolvable). Re-measured on `origin/main` `900f8d995`, `packages/plugin-list/src/ListView.tsx`:

- the gate is at **`:2084`**, its dependency array at **`:2155`**, the `case 'chart'` render branch at **`:2608`** (the card's numbers were taken on an older tip and are ±0 here);
- **seven** visualizations had a capability check — kanban, gallery, calendar, timeline, gantt, map, tree — and **`chart` had none**. The dependency array told the same story independently: seven binding blocks plus the whitelist, no `schema.chart`.

So a `grid` view that declared a complete `chart:` block and whitelisted `['grid', 'chart']` had its own whitelist filtered down to nothing and fell back to `['grid']`. `chart` reached the offered set only through the "always allow switching back to the schema's own viewType" leg — i.e. only when the view was already `viewType: 'chart'`. Both halves were spec-legal the whole time (`VisualizationTypeSchema` lists `chart`; `chart:` is `ListChartConfigSchema` on the list view). Only the gate never asked.

This is `map`'s #5042 one visualization over, and is fixed the same way.

## The change

One new module-level resolver, `resolveListChartBinding`, sitting beside `resolveListMapConfig`, and **both** readers go through it:

- `case 'chart'` routes on its `shape` and reads its fields;
- the capability gate reads its `resolves`.

The gate carries **no second copy** of the predicate — that requirement is the point of the ruling on #7544, and the drift class it names (#7495) is exactly what a copied condition becomes. `schema.chart` also joins the memo's dependency array, so a block that arrives on a later render is seen rather than answered from the first render's schema.

`resolves` is the "binds to names the **author** wrote" question, one leg per shape:

| shape | resolves when |
|:--|:--|
| ADR-0021 (#1890) | `dataset` present **and** at least one measure in `values` (dimensions may legitimately be absent — a single aggregate) |
| legacy | a declared category (`xAxisField` / `categoryField`) **and** a declared measure (`yAxisFields[0]` / `valueField`) — exactly what the legacy leg reads *before* its floors |

Precedence is the render branch's existing one, inherited rather than re-decided: the view-level block replaces the legacy `options.chart` bag wholesale (`||`), which is what `chart` and `tree` already do.

**Render behaviour is unchanged.** The routing test is still `chartCfg.dataset`'s truthiness, the dataset leg emits the same seven properties from the same values, and the legacy leg's `'name'` / `'value'` floors stay literally where they were — the resolver simply reports the declared values and the branch applies the floors. Those floors are #7547 (the #7029 / #7070 family), ruled out of scope by the card and untouched here. They are also *why* the negative half below matters: with nothing declared the legacy leg still returns a chart, bound to names nobody authored, so the switcher must not offer a route into it.

## Evidence

New suite `packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/ListView.chart-capability-7544.test.tsx` — the card's seven-positive/one-negative probe table turned into landed tests, both directions pinned.

**Before the fix**, on `900f8d995` with the suite added and the source untouched:

```
Tests  8 failed | 22 passed (30)
× offers Chart for a complete ADR-0021 block
× offers Chart for the legacy `xAxisField` / `yAxisFields` block
× offers Chart for the legacy `categoryField` / `valueField` spelling
× CONTROL: the legacy `options.chart` bag resolves the capability too
× CONTROL: the view-level block wins over the bag, as the render branch resolves it
× recomputes when the chart block arrives on a later render
× an offered ADR-0021 block renders from the author names
× an offered legacy block renders from the author names
```

The 22 that already passed are the load-bearing half: all **fourteen** sibling-control arms (kanban / gallery / calendar / timeline / gantt / map / tree, offered with a binding **and** withheld without one), every `chart` negative arm (no block, empty block, `chartType` only, `dataset` with no measure, a legacy half-binding either way), the untouched schema-viewType leg, and the render-branch floor pin. `chart` was the only visualization answering "no" with its block declared.

**After** (`pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-list/src/__tests__/ListView.chart-capability-7544.test.tsx`, from the repo root): `Test Files 1 passed (1) · Tests 30 passed (30)`.

**Ablation** — the new capability check deleted, resolver and render branch left in place, implementation committed first:

```
HEAD_BLOB=39829e5e958ce92ef0cad76f73f19994377cb874   BEFORE_HASH=39829e5e...cb874
GATE_BEFORE=1 MARK_BEFORE=0  ->  GATE_AFTER=0 MARK_AFTER=1   AFTER_HASH=aba07af0...7120
MUTATION_CONFIRMED_ON_DISK
Tests  8 failed | 22 passed (30)     <- the pre-fix reading, exactly
RESTORED_HASH=39829e5e...cb874 == HEAD_BLOB · GIT_DIFF_HEAD_BYTES=0 · GATE_RESTORED=1 MARK_RESTORED=0
RESTORATION_PROVEN_BY_STATE
```

The failures name themselves (`… > the capability gate resolves 'chart' from a declared chart block (objectui#7544) > offers Chart for a complete ADR-0021 block`). No build step is involved on either leg: the suite imports the mutated file relatively (`../ListView`), so the mutation is in the code under test by construction rather than by a `dist` round-trip. Restore ran under a `trap … EXIT INT TERM` with absolute paths and is proven by state, not by an exit code.

**Union re-run at the final commit `1a3ef5c21`** (working tree clean, so the heavy legs below ran on byte-identical content):

| check | verdict line |
|:--|:--|
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-list/` | `Test Files 67 passed (67) · Tests 852 passed (852)` |
| `turbo run type-check --filter @object-ui/plugin-list` | `Tasks: 14 successful, 14 total` (the package's script is `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so the new suite is type-checked too) |
| `turbo run lint --filter @object-ui/plugin-list` | `✖ 474 problems (0 errors, 474 warnings)` — exit 0; the new file contributes 5 `no-explicit-any` warnings, the same kind and count-per-line the sibling `ListView.*.test.tsx` files already carry |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | before: `❌ 1 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change adds no changeset` → after: `✅ 2 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change declares 1 changeset(s): .changeset/7544-listview-chart-capability-gate.md.` |
| `pnpm changeset:check` | `✅ All workspace packages are in the changeset fixed group.` · `✅ No changeset declares a major bump.` (this one is `patch`) |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | `✅ check-control-bytes: OK (scanned 6362 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary).` |

**Not run, stated plainly:** the repo-wide `pnpm lint` / `pnpm test` farm and the sibling packages' suites (`app-shell`, `plugin-view`, `apps/console`). The change is confined to `ListView.tsx`'s own gate and render branch; a grep over every non-`plugin-list` test that renders `ListView` and mentions `chart` found only `plugin-view`'s own `ObjectView` branches, which have a separate switcher and are untouched. CI runs the farm exactly once.

## Scope

`packages/plugin-list` only. No key, no exported symbol and no accept set moves — `packages/types`, the zod mirrors and `@objectstack/spec` are not touched (clause-② stays `no`). The `xAxisKey`/value floors at `ListView.tsx` and `plugin-view/src/ObjectView.tsx` are left alone: that is #7547 and out of scope here.
